Summary: He looks down at the mess, trying to figure out what he'd been doing shoving a box full of papers up there. He notices handwriting on several pieces of loose paper and he wonders if maybe Chris has been storing away his assignments or bits of homework. Eddie rolls his eyes at himself when he realizes that he's still staring down at the box and its contents on the floor, rather than bending to scoop it up. Bending down, he scoops up a handful of papers and looks closely at them; his heart sinks when he recognizes the handwriting on the loose sheets of paper.The loose sheets are all neat, sloping cursive, some in Bobby's familiar handwriting: his 6-cheese lasagna, the mac and cheese that Bobby jokingly said should only be saved for momentous occasions... There's even a recipe for something called 'Athena's Angel Cake'.--Cleaning up some of Christopher's old belongings, Eddie comes across an unfamiliar box in the crawl space of his ceiling. The box is full of recipes and a stack of letters that have all been addressed and dated, but never posted.

entry.title: How you could be gone?
entry.summary:
Author: DylanGArgent

Rating: Teen And Up AudiencesLanguage: EnglishWords: 34,687Chapters: 13/?Kudos: 343

Summary: Evan Buckley knew he had never belonged to the Buckleys; something inside him said he wasn't part of that family. Maybe it was the toy fire truck he held in his hand, which he had always had and remembered, that whispered there was something more he didn't know could exist. The initials carved into the truck, R. N., made him wish he knew what they meant. Perhaps, in time, he could find himself. Bobby Nash wanted to be angry, but what he really felt was worry. Buck was always reckless, rebellious, and never took care of himself, which terrified Bobby. He wanted to protect him, not knowing if the real reason was because he saw Buck in the little boy he lost years ago, or perhaps the mark that looked so much like his baby son's—though he knew it could just be a coincidence, because that's how things happened: coincidences. Buck couldn't possibly be Robin Nash.
